title: Math, math everywhere
statementMd:
*If you have gone that far, you'll probably skip unnecessary legends anyway...*

You are given a binary string ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/b867005672a53a90079685a121443181793694d7.png) and an integer ![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/be942ae2800fe456a9cd1c9c63aa053db9c70c46.png). Find the number of integers $*k*$, $0 ≤ *k* < *N*$, such that for all $*i* = 0$, $1$, ..., $*m* - 1$

![image](https://espresso.codeforces.com/ada0566abcbcd6a3f78b0d17aecbd2f9f26a8ec8.png)

Print the answer modulo

10<sup>9</sup> + 7

.

## Input

In the first line of input there is a string $*s*$ consisting of $0$'s and $1$'s ($1 ≤ |*s*| ≤ 40$).

In the next line of input there is an integer $*n*$ ($1 ≤ *n* ≤ 5·10^{5}$).

Each of the next $*n*$ lines contains two space-separated integers $*p*_{*i*}$, $α_{*i*}$ ($1 ≤ *p*_{*i*}, α_{*i*} ≤ 10^{9}$, $*p*_{*i*}$ is prime). All $*p*_{*i*}$ are distinct.

## Output

A single integer — the answer to the problem.
